title: Session Stack: Trust Boundary Mapping
description: Map the VTAM → TSO → RFE session layers. Identify where identity is bound and trust shifts.

steps.title: Connect to Mainframe
steps.description: Establish a TN3270 connection to the mainframe.
steps.screen:
Connecting to mainframe via TN3270...

Establishing LU session with VTAM.
The session fabric exists independently of TCP/IP.
steps.hint: The session is managed by VTAM, not the network stack. Your LU session can outlive the TCP connection.

steps.title: VTAM Entry Screen
steps.description: You are at the VTAM session manager - anonymous, no identity bound yet.
steps.screen:
MVS 3.8j TK5   IP: localhost:3270

   M   M  V   V  SSSSS
   MM MM  V   V  S
   M M M  V   V  SSSSS
   M   M   V V       S
   M   M    V   SSSSS

 ===> _

Enter TSO to logon
steps.expected: Identify the VTAM session fabric - you are anonymous with no identity bound.
steps.hint: Press Enter to see the logon prompt. This is the session manager itself, not a service on a port.

steps.title: TSO Logon - Identity Binding
steps.description: Log in to TSO to bind your identity. RAKF verifies the password.
steps.screen:
TSO/E LOGON

Userid ===> HERC01
Password ===> ********

Procedure ===> IKJACCNT
steps.expected: VTAM routes session to TSO. Enter userid and password.
steps.hint: VTAM acts as a session router. The transition from VTAM to TSO is a control-plane boundary crossing. TK5 uses RAKF for security, not RACF.

steps.title: TSO READY Prompt
steps.description: You are now at the TSO command line with identity bound.
steps.expected: Reach TSO READY prompt. Your identity (HERC01) is now bound to this address space.
steps.hint: Every command at TSO READY runs under HERC01's authority. There is no sudo - your authority is determined by RAKF profiles.

steps.title: Enter RFE (ISPF-like)
steps.description: Enter RFE, the RPF Full-screen Editor - TK5's ISPF equivalent.
steps.screen:
RFE - MVS 3.8j Turnkey System

Option ===>_

0  Settings     1  Browse      2  Edit
3  Utilities    4  Foreground  5  Batch
6  Command      7  Dialog      8  LM

F1=Help  F3=Exit
steps.expected: Enter RFE panel interface. Your TSO address space persists - identity context survives across panels.
steps.hint: TK5 uses RFE, not modern ISPF. Job output is viewed via TSO OUTPUT command, not SDSF.

steps.title: LISTALC - View Allocated Datasets
steps.description: See what datasets are allocated to your session.
steps.screen:
READY

LISTALC STATUS

--DDNAME   DISP
  STEPLIB
           KEEP   SYS1.CMDLIB
  SYSPROC
           KEEP   SYSC.CMDPROC

READY
steps.expected: View dataset allocations - the resource context of your identity.
steps.hint: LISTALC STATUS shows every dataset allocated to this TSO session. STEPLIB controls which programs are available.

steps.title: STATUS - View Your Jobs
steps.description: Check status of jobs you have submitted.
steps.screen:
READY

STATUS

IKJ56192I NO JOB STATUS AVAILABLE FOR HERC01

READY
steps.expected: View job status. No jobs running means no batch work in the JES queue.
steps.hint: STATUS shows jobs in the JES2 queue. Use OUTPUT to view completed job output.

steps.title: Exit RFE to TSO
steps.description: Exit RFE and return to TSO READY prompt.
steps.hint: PF3 or X exits panels. At the RFE Primary Menu, X returns to TSO READY.

steps.title: LOGOFF - Return to VTAM
steps.description: Log off TSO to unbind identity and return to VTAM.
steps.screen:
READY

LOGOFF

IKJ56470I HERC01 LOGGED OFF TSO AT 14:32:00 ON MAY 28, 2026

MVS 3.8j TK5

 ===> _
steps.expected: Logoff from TSO - identity is unbound, returning to anonymous VTAM session.
steps.hint: Never disconnect while logged in - it locks the userid. Recover with /C U=userid at Hercules console. Three control planes traversed: VTAM → TSO → RFE.
